guide.explain: Which environment this resource runs in.
guide.format: one of prod, uat, dev, test

rules.message: Add environment: prod, uat, dev or test.

guide.explain: Only the four approved environments are allowed.

rules.message: environment must be prod, uat, dev or test (e.g. production → prod).

guide.explain: The product this resource belongs to. Billing is grouped by it.
guide.format: the app's one canonical name, lowercase with hyphens

rules.message: Add application with the app's canonical name.

guide.explain: Use exactly the same app name everywhere so billing doesn't split.
guide.format: matches the org's canonical app list

check.question: Is this value one of the org's canonical application names, or an obvious variant of one?

rules.message: This looks like a variant of a canonical app name. Use the canonical one.

guide.explain: What this resource does inside the app.
guide.format: prefer api, frontend, backend, db, cache, worker, queue, storage, lb

guide.explain: Stick to the standard component names where one fits.
guide.format: api | frontend | backend | db | cache | worker | queue | storage | lb

rules.message: Prefer a standard component name such as api or worker.

guide.explain: The team or person responsible for cost, patching and cleanup.

rules.message: Add owner with your first name or team.
Label values can't contain @ or dots. Use a team or first name, e.g. owner=pranit.

guide.explain: How this resource is managed, so nobody's console edits get overwritten by Terraform.

rules.message: Add managed-by. You're creating this in the console, so use manual.

guide.explain: Only three values are allowed. Ownership goes in owner, not here.

rules.message: managed-by must be terraform, manual or gcp.

guide.explain: Keys and values use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.

rules.message: Use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only (max 63 characters).

guide.explain: Grant the smallest role that does the job.
guide.format: a predefined role, never Owner or Editor

rules.message: Least privilege: don't grant Owner or Editor. Grant the requested role instead.

guide.explain: Service account keys are long-lived secrets. Cloud Run uses the attached service account instead.

rules.message: You don't need a key for Cloud Run. Attach the service account to the service instead.

guide.explain: Company Policy requires Production mode. Firebase warns that Test mode allows anyone to read and overwrite your data.

rules.message: Test mode allows anyone to read and overwrite your data. Choose Start in Production mode before Create.
